title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k) its Witt vectors, and ν ≥ 1 an integer. Grothendieck wants an initial object in the category of artinian local rings with residue field k whose maximal ideal carries ν-nilpotent divided powers. Since p must lie in the PD ideal, one formally adjoins the divided powers Λ_i = γ_{p^i}(Λ_0) for 0 ≤ i ≤ ν. The defining relations are
- Λ_i^p = u_i Λ_{i+1}, where u_i = (p^{i+1})!/((p^i)!)^p;
- Λ_ν^p = 0, which expresses ν-nilpotence;
- Λ_0 = p.
The result is called W^{(ν)}. Primes ℓ ≠ p are invertible in W, so only the γ_{p^i} need to be adjoined.

Computation. First drop the relation Λ_0 = p and work in A^{(ν)}. Put λ_i = γ_{p^i}(p) = p^{p^i}/(p^i)! ∈ W and Λ_i = λ_i + Θ_i. A^{(ν)} is free over W on the monomials Θ_0^{a_0}…Θ_ν^{a_ν} with 0 ≤ a_i ≤ p−1. W^{(ν)} is then A^{(ν)}/I, where I = (Θ_0).

Lemma. An element Σ_a w_a Θ^a lies in I if and only if:
- (a) for every a ≠ 0 whose first nonzero component is a_i, w_a ∈ p^i W;
- (b) the constant coefficient w_0 lies in p^{c(ν)} W, where c(ν) = ν + p[p^ν − (p^{ν−1}+…+1)] = ν + p·v_p(λ_ν).

Proof of sufficiency. It suffices to show p^i Θ_i ∈ I for all i and p^{c(ν)} ∈ I.
- Induction on i. Since λ_i^p = u_i λ_{i+1} holds already in W, the relation (Θ_i+λ_i)^p = u_i(Θ_{i+1}+λ_{i+1}) reduces to Σ_{α≥1} C(p,α) Θ_i^α λ_i^{p−α} = u_i Θ_{i+1}.
- Multiply by p^i. Because p^iΘ_i ∈ I, the left side lies in I, so p^i u_i Θ_{i+1} ∈ I.
- Since v_p(u_i) = 1, u_i is p times a unit, giving p^{i+1}Θ_{i+1} ∈ I.
- The next page does the same with (λ_ν+Θ_ν)^p = 0 to get p^ν λ_ν^p ∈ I, and v_p(p^ν λ_ν^p) = c(ν).

Necessity (next page). The set I' cut out by conditions (a) and (b) is an ideal containing Θ_0, and it is contained in I; the ideal check is left to the reader.

Corollary (next page). W^{(ν)} has an explicit normal form: monomials in Θ_1..Θ_ν with exponents ≤ p−1. A monomial whose first nonzero exponent is in position i gets a coefficient in W/p^i. The constant term gets a coefficient in W/p^{c(ν)}. Hence W^{(ν)} is artinian, with length c(ν) + Σ_i i·(p−1)p^{ν−i} over W.

This gives a concrete universal 'nilpotent-PD' thickening of k over W. It serves the foundations of crystalline cohomology (crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1965–69), where the nilpotence condition on divided powers matters.
errors: Minor abuse: writes p^iΘ_i^α = 0 and p^i u_i Θ_{i+1} = 0 where 'in I' (i.e. zero in the quotient W^{(ν)}) is meant; harmless.
Sufficiency only shows each monomial generator lies in I; one also needs that I is closed under W-linear combinations, which is trivial.
The 'first nonzero component' convention assumes indexing starting at a_0. For monomials with a_0 ≠ 0 the condition w_a ∈ p^0W is vacuous, consistent with Θ_0 ∈ I.

Necessity is only sketched ('laissée au lecteur'). I checked it on the main cases: Θ_i^p reduces with cancelling constant term for i < ν, and for i = ν the constant is −λ_ν^p, giving exactly the p^{c(ν)} condition. It appears correct.
Sanity check p=2, ν=1: W^{(1)} = W/8 ⊕ (W/2)Θ_1 with Θ_1^2 = −4, and c(1) = 3. Consistent.
The next-page corollary as transcribed omits the constant-term coefficient range W/p^{c(ν)}.

ideas.what: Initial object in the category of artinian local W-algebras with residue field k and ν-nilpotent divided powers on the maximal ideal, constructed as a truncated PD-polynomial algebra W⟨x⟩ (generated by γ_{p^i}(x), i ≤ ν, with γ_{p^ν}(x)^p = 0) specialised at x = p.
ideas.modern_name: Truncated / nilpotent PD-envelope; universal PD-nilpotent thickening of k
ideas.usually_credited_to: PD-nilpotence: Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974), Grothendieck ('Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', IHES 1966/68)
ideas.where_published: Nilpotent divided powers are discussed in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés); this explicit universal ring is not known to me there

ideas.what: Change of variables Λ_i = γ_{p^i}(p) + Θ_i giving a W-basis of monomials with exponents < p, and an explicit description of the ideal (Θ_0).
ideas.modern_name: Explicit structure of divided-power algebras over Z_p (normal form)

ideas.what: Valuation identity v_p((p^{i+1})!/((p^i)!)^p) = 1 and v_p(γ_{p^ν}(p)) = p^ν − (p^ν−1)/(p−1), via Legendre's formula.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre's formula; p-adic valuation of divided powers

ideas.what: Explicit invariant c(ν) = ν + p(p^ν − (p^ν−1)/(p−1)): the exact power of p killed in the universal ν-nilpotent PD thickening.
ideas.modern_name: p-torsion exponent of a nilpotent PD-envelope

missed.claim: An explicit computation of the universal artinian W-algebra with ν-nilpotent PD maximal ideal: a normal form with coefficients in W/p^i, plus the exact constant-term torsion exponent c(ν). This computation does not appear to be recorded in the crystalline literature, which uses nilpotent PD structures abstractly.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a concrete universal base for nilpotent-PD crystalline sites over k, and quantitative torsion bounds of the kind relevant to integral/torsion comparison questions. The interest is modest; specialists could rederive it easily.

missed.claim: The page does not discuss the behaviour of the tower W^{(ν)} as ν varies (transition maps, the pro-system and its limit). That limit would be a pro-artinian universal PD-nilpotent base, and its role in the crystal formalism is not developed here.
missed.quote: On va construire un objet initial de cette catégorie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild loose end. Comparing this pro-object with W itself, with the p-adic PD structure on p not being nilpotent, is a small point in the foundations of nilpotent crystalline sites.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct, careful and explicit, but it is a technical lemma inside the well-known development of crystalline foundations (nilpotent divided powers). Specialists would find it natural rather than surprising, even though this exact normal form and c(ν) are probably not printed anywhere.
